newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest despite a small hike in the interbank rate, dealers said Wednesday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at 0.85/0.80 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 0.90/0.85 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.44/1.39 percent against 1.48/1.43 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.15/99.20 from Tuesday's close of S$99.08/99.13, September 2001 at S$97.37/97.42 versus S$97.35/40 and June 2003 at S$95.37/95.42 against $S95.35/95.40.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/8 3 percent from Tuesday's 2-3/8 2-1/4 percent.
